sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Port Huron, Michigan?
sections.html:
Port Huron sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an offer from a company that buys houses directly. The city is the seat of St. Clair County, and the county's land records office is inside the city.

Speed in this market comes from how much is left to settle. A house with a clear title, permits on file and no tenant can close quickly under any route. One with an unpaid tax bill, a missing permit or a lease in place takes longer, and a buyer will either wait for you to fix it or lower the price. The sections below cover what Port Huron and St. Clair County require so you can clear those items early.

sections.h2: Where is Port Huron and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Port Huron sits at the point where Lake Huron drains into the St. Clair River, directly across from Sarnia, Ontario. The Blue Water Bridge joins the two cities at the eastern end of I-69 and I-94. The city covers 12.26 square miles, but only 8.08 of those are land, and the Black River divides the city in half before it empties into the St. Clair River near downtown (Wikipedia, Port Huron).

The U.S. built Fort Gratiot here in 1814, the city incorporated in 1857, and in 1871 it became the county seat. A fire burned the city on October 8, 1871, and an F4 tornado on May 21, 1953 damaged or destroyed more than 400 structures. In 1895 the village of Fort Gratiot was annexed. Shipbuilding and lumber work pulled in immigrants in the 1850s, and auto-parts makers followed in later years.

The Census Bureau counted 28,983 people in 2020 and estimates 28,273 for July 1, 2025, a 2.4% decline from the 2020 base. With 8.10 square miles of land that works out to 3,577.3 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Port Huron homes?
sections.html:
Port Huron's median owner-occupied home value was $149,300 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Median gross rent was $982, and 61.7% of homes were lived in by their owners.

  • Households: 12,734, with 2.21 persons per household.
  • Median household income: $50,366.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,140; without one: $562.
  • Residents aged 65 or older: 18.0%, the highest share of the four cities in this set.
  • Mean commute: 20.8 minutes.

A house inherited from an older relative needs its title and probate steps finished before it can be listed, so start those early.

sections.h2: How do Port Huron winters and the waterfront affect a house?
sections.html:
The NOAA 1991 to 2020 normals give Port Huron 34.87 inches of precipitation and 35.5 inches of snow a year, with 22 snowy days. January is the coldest month, with an average low of 19.9 F, and the record low is minus 19 F. The average July high is 81.3 F.

Because so much of the city touches water, flood zones matter. Port Huron's planning page links flood maps, and the building page warns that a property in a flood plain or zone may need approval from the state's EGLE Water Resources division for exterior projects. Ask the Building Inspection Division whether your parcel is mapped before you list.

sections.h2: What draws buyers to Port Huron?
sections.html:
Water access is the main draw. The city owns 17 waterfront areas covering 102 acres with 3.5 miles of water frontage, three public beaches and the largest municipal marina system in Michigan, with five mooring locations. It also has 14 public parks and a community center.

Jobs come from auto-parts makers such as SMR Automotive and International Automotive Components, plus two acute care hospitals, McLaren Port Huron and Lake Huron Medical Center. St. Clair County Community College is in the city, and Port Huron High School and Port Huron Northern High School serve students.

sections.h2: Which Port Huron permits matter before a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Building Inspection page lists what needs a permit, and a buyer's inspector often checks the same items. The table sorts the common ones.

Port Huron permit categories from the city's building page
Permit typeExamples listed
Building permitRoofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, porches, garages, basement finishes, interior and exterior alterations
Zoning permitFences, driveways, concrete patios, hot tubs, playground equipment, pools over 24 inches deep
Mechanical permitFurnaces, air conditioners, hot water tanks, fireplaces, gas piping
Electrical permitNew circuits, water heaters, sump pumps, generators, smoke detectors
No permit neededPainting, carpeting, tile, replacing kitchen cabinets in the same layout

The city lists what happens without a permit: safety problems, fines, possibly tearing the structure down, and, in its words, permit issues if you decide to sell. A homeowner may pull permits in place of a contractor only if they are the registered legal owner and live in the house as their primary residence. Properties in the Historic District need Historic District Commission approval for exterior work. Contact the Building Inspection Division at (810) 984-9733.

sections.h2: Does Port Huron regulate rental or vacant houses?
sections.html:
Yes. The city runs a Rental Certification Program through its planning department, and the planning page posts a Foreclosed, Vacant and Abandoned Property Registration Form. If you are selling a house that has been rented or sits empty, ask the Building Inspection Division what registration or certification applies to the address and whether it transfers to a buyer.

The city also lists the Port Huron Historic District ordinance, Chapter 52-576 through 52-591, for properties inside that district.

sections.h2: What does the St. Clair County Register of Deeds do at closing?
sections.html:
The St. Clair County Register of Deeds is at 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103, Port Huron, and its phone number is (810) 989-6930. It is open Monday through Thursday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and Friday from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closing 12:00 to 1:00 each day. The recording counter closes at 4:00 p.m., and a document received after that is dated 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

  • Recording fee: $30.00 per document regardless of page count, plus $3.00 after the first instrument reference.
  • Certification of a recorded copy: $5.00 per document.
  • Tax certificate: needed before recording a warranty deed, land contract, or a deed with a warranty covenant (MCL 211.135). The treasurer certifies over the counter from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., closed noon to 1:00 p.m.
  • Transfer tax as printed by the county: $1.10 per thousand dollars of the sale amount on the deed for the county, and $7.50 per thousand for the state.

Land records are viewable online from 1984 to the present, and the office offers a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Most sellers let the title company take the deed in for recording.

faqs.q: How fast can I close on a house in Port Huron?
faqs.a: It depends on title, taxes and any tenant. At the recording end, the St. Clair County counter closes at 4:00 p.m., and a document received after that is dated 8:00 a.m. the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work I did before selling in Port Huron?
faqs.a: Roofs, windows, doors, siding, decks, garages and basement finishes need a building permit, and furnaces, water heaters and sump pumps need trade permits. Skipping one can cause problems at sale time, according to the city's own page.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Port Huron house?
faqs.a: Record it with the St. Clair County Register of Deeds at 200 Grand River Avenue, Suite 103. The recording fee is $30.00, and a warranty deed needs a tax certificate from the county treasurer first.

faqs.q: What is the St. Clair County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds fee page prints $1.10 per thousand dollars of the sale amount for the county and $7.50 per thousand for the state. Your settlement statement shows the exact figures for your sale.

faqs.q: Does Port Huron have flood zones that affect a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The city links flood maps on its planning page, and a property in a flood plain may need state approval for exterior projects. Ask the Building Inspection Division at (810) 984-9733 whether your parcel is mapped.
